preamble: Nasalization of the open vowel /a/ to [ã] happens when the velum lowers in anticipation of a neighbouring nasal consonant. If the conditioning nasal is later lost, the nasality stays on the vowel as a contrastive feature. Examples are Portuguese lã 'wool' (< Latin lāna), Hindi dā̃t 'tooth' and Bengali cãd 'moon' (< Sanskrit danta, candra), and Old Lithuanian ą (< Balto-Slavic *an), which was a nasal vowel before it denasalized.
phoneticEffects: Nasalization, Regressive Assimilation, Nasal Consonant Loss, Phonemicization

examples.note: Intervocalic /n/ nasalized the preceding /a/ and was lost (Old Galician-Portuguese lãa > lã); the modern vowel is a raised nasal [ɐ̃].
Intervocalic /n/ was absorbed into the preceding /a/ as nasality and then lost.
The nasal of the cluster -nt- was absorbed into the preceding vowel, which became long and nasalized.
The nasal of the cluster -nd- was absorbed into the preceding vowel, which became long and nasalized.
The chandrabindu marks the nasal vowel left by the lost cluster nasal.
This is the same nasal absorption as in Hindi dā̃t.

examples.note: Tautosyllabic *an became a nasal vowel, written with the ogonek; it later denasalized to long [aː].
